title: Quebec Invites 790 Skilled Worker Candidates for Permanent Residency Selection
excerpt: The province issued invitations across all four PSTQ streams on August 27, targeting healthcare, engineering, trades and exceptional talent occupations.
body:
• Quebec issued 790 invitations on August 27 under all four streams of the Skilled Worker Selection Program (PSTQ), the province's eighth draw of 2026.
  • Stream 2 (intermediate and manual skills) received the most invitations at 324, targeting healthcare, education, construction and transportation occupations.
  • Cutoff scores ranged from 393 to 710 depending on the stream and exercise, with priority given to workers already residing in Quebec.
  • PSTQ invitation volumes are being scaled back until October 31 to accommodate the reopened Quebec Experience Program (PEQ).

Quebec's Ministry of Immigration, Francisation and Integration (MIFI) issued 790 invitations to apply for permanent selection on August 27, marking the province's eighth draw under the Skilled Worker Selection Program (PSTQ) this year.

Candidate profiles were extracted from the Arrima portal on August 24 at 11:48 a.m. for selections across all four streams. Those selected can now submit complete applications for a Quebec Selection Certificate (CSQ), which enables a federal permanent residence application with the intent to settle in Quebec.

How the Invitations Were Distributed

Stream 2, covering intermediate and manual skills at TEER 3–5 levels, accounted for the largest share with 324 invitations across four exercises. Candidates needed 24 months of work experience in the last five years, including 12 months in Quebec. Priority occupations included nurse aides, teacher assistants, home support workers, cooks, truck drivers and construction trades workers. Cutoff scores ranged from 616 to 706.

Stream 3, for regulated professions, issued 109 invitations targeting healthcare workers, engineers, skilled tradespeople and transportation professionals. Exercise 1 alone covered 32 healthcare and education occupations, from general practitioners and registered nurses to dentists and veterinarians, with a cutoff score of 639.

Stream 1, for highly qualified and specialized workers in TEER 0–2 occupations, accounted for 87 invitations. The draw targeted healthcare professionals, natural scientists, cybersecurity specialists, data scientists, engineering managers and various engineering and manufacturing roles. Cutoff scores ranged from 639 to 710.

Stream 4, for exceptional talent, rounded out the draw with 21 invitations. These went to candidates with positive opinion letters from MIFI partners or those with qualifying exceptional achievements combined with a doctorate-level education.

Context: The PEQ Factor

The current PSTQ invitation strategy reflects a deliberate reduction in volumes following the July 2 reopening of the Quebec Experience Program (PEQ), the province's flagship permanent residence pathway that had been suspended.

Until October 31, when the PEQ's first intake period closes, Quebec is concentrating PSTQ invitations among candidates in TEER 4 and 5 occupations and those who have not yet accumulated two years of work experience. Starting in November 2026, PSTQ invitation levels will be adjusted based on PEQ application volumes to remain within the 2026–2029 immigration plan targets.

"Quebec has said it intends to issue the same number of CSQs across both programs for the remainder of the period covered by its 2026–2029 immigration plan."

— CIC News

What This Means for Indian Applicants

With 14,545 candidates invited across eight draws in 2026, Quebec continues to actively recruit skilled workers despite the reduced PSTQ volumes. Indian professionals in healthcare, engineering, IT and skilled trades who already reside in Quebec are well-positioned to benefit, particularly those with French language proficiency and occupations in priority sectors.

Prospective candidates who have not yet registered should submit a declaration of interest through the Arrima portal. Profiles remain valid for one year and are assessed against factors including occupation, French language skills, education, Quebec work experience and age.

What's Next

The interplay between the PSTQ and PEQ will shape Quebec's immigration landscape through the end of the decade. After the PEQ's first intake closes on October 31, Quebec will recalibrate both programs to balance permanent residence selections under its multi-year plan. Candidates with strong French skills and in-province work experience will likely continue to receive priority in future draws.
